source.title: Relative Scaling Laws for LLMs
source.authors: William B. Held; D. Hall; Percy Liang; Di-Yi Yang

page_placements.theme: Aggregate gains conceal instance, subgroup and distributional differences

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: It evaluates scaling and predictability on downstream benchmarks and subgroup distributions, using downstream losses, accuracy, and risk-evaluation probabilities rather than the original studies’ held-out pretraining-loss measurements.
record.gate_note: The paper cites classical pretraining scaling laws but does not report its own held-out pretraining cross-entropy results or test parameter/token/compute exponents and compute-optimal allocation trends. Rows below cover its own downstream predictability results and its own scaling measurements of language variation and AI-risk evaluations; cited results are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study fits compute-to-loss power laws on downstream task losses (MMLU, and Gemstones benchmarks in App. C) along compute-optimal IsoFLOP runs. It then maps loss to accuracy, validated on held-out external models. This bears directly on V6. It does not report pretraining-loss exponents, compute-optimal allocation exponents, shape ablations or extrapolation tests, so V1–V5 and V7 are untested. Its main relative-scaling results (subgroup gaps, risk clusters) are a different construct.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that relative scaling laws separate initial disparity from improvement rate. Scale is not a universal equalizer: MMLU domains converge, regional Englishes diverge, and capability- or influence-related risks are amplified while adversarial ones are not. With a careful protocol (modified MCQ, two-stage fit), downstream accuracy is predictable from compute.
record.recipe_differences: The study introduces relative scaling based on treatment-to-baseline error ratios and trains an IsoFLOP suite using the Qwen 3 architecture; it does not reproduce the original studies' absolute pretraining-loss fitting procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: MMLU loss–compute predictability changes with prompt format. In language-variation evaluations, model-size scaling shifts regional relative performance while token scaling leaves relative ordering nearly unchanged. Risk trajectories also vary by training dataset.

fits_no_version.finding: AI-risk evaluation likelihoods scale differently by cluster and corpus. Capability- and influence-related clusters rise with compute; Scheming and Incorrigibility stay flat or decline.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Risk-evaluation response likelihood does not change uniformly across categories as pretraining compute increases.

fits_no_version.finding: Relative loss gaps between MMLU topic groups shrink toward parity with compute on all three corpora.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Subgroup loss disparities on knowledge domains narrow with compute-optimal scaling.

fits_no_version.finding: Relative BPB gaps between regional Englishes and U.S. English narrow, stay flat or widen. The relative slope correlates with online speaker population (R 0.82–0.84). Model-size scaling, not token scaling, drives the shifts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Scaling does not uniformly close distributional gaps; the gap trend depends on subgroup representation and on whether parameters or data are scaled.

record.code_released: Marin GitHub and a separate analysis/plotting project repository are stated; URLs not stated in the text.
record.problems: The study uses selective case studies; authors note that raw language-model loss may not reflect broad downstream utility. Several reported curve values are presented in figures rather than specified in text. The study does not test the original claim's held-out pretraining-loss laws or compute-optimal allocation exponents.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows left out. Figure-only endpoint values for MMLU, English varieties, and risk curves were not transcribed when the text did not provide a value that could be assigned reliably.

untested.parts: No held-out pretraining-loss power-law fits or exponents in parameters, tokens or compute. ICE BPB falls with compute (Fig. 5a), but no fit on the pretraining distribution is reported.
No test of predicting much larger runs' loss from small-run fits. The 8B model is used to fit the calibration, not held out as an extrapolation target.
IsoFLOP sweeps pick compute-optimal points, but no growth exponents for parameters or tokens are reported.
Depth is set by a fixed rule; no shape ablation.
No other modalities, repeated data or fine-tuning.
No comparison of fitting methods, parameter counting or schedules for the loss laws. The optimizer comparison (App. B) is relative BPB, not exponent dependence.

missing.what: Per-benchmark R² of Gemstones downstream loss–compute fits (about 0.77–0.92; Winogrande about 0.49)
Loss-to-accuracy sigmoid calibration across DCLM Core MCQ tasks

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked relative-gap rows to V6 and marked widening gaps 'reversed'. That misreads V6: absolute performance improves for every subgroup, and gap direction is a separate construct. Prompt-format rows bear on V6 protocol dependence, not V7. Appendix B's optimizer comparison (Muon's early gain flattens with scale) is relative BPB and was not linked to any version.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss power laws in parameters, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of much larger runs from power laws fitted on smaller runs.
Growth exponents for compute-optimal parameter and token counts, and whether the split follows either published trend.
Effect of varying architecture details at fixed parameter count.
Power-law behavior in other modalities or training regimes such as repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer.
Downstream benchmarks and evaluations beyond those reported here; the paper does not establish predictability for downstream tasks generally.

The study shows sensitivity to evaluation prompt format, but does not test parameter-counting conventions, alternative fitting methods for the original pretraining laws, or compute-optimal allocation exponents. It does not report systematic bending of held-out pretraining-loss curves.

relationships.condition: Modified-MCQ or continuation MMLU loss along compute-optimal runs; two-stage compute→loss→accuracy; Gemstones downstream losses (most tasks)
relationships.reason: MMLU loss scales with compute (R² 0.61–0.68, r1, r3). Topic-group losses fall log-linearly on all three corpora (r6–r8). Loss→accuracy holds on held-out Llama 3, OLMo 2 and Qwen 3 (r4). Gemstones task losses fit power laws (r5).
relationships.display_finding: MMLU compute–loss fits achieved R² of 0.61–0.68, topic losses fell log-linearly across three corpora, Gemstones task losses followed power laws, and loss predicted held-out Llama 3, OLMo 2, and Qwen 3 accuracy.
